title: Online unsupervised industrial anomaly detection with adaptive resonance patch prototype memory and multi-level views
content:
by Yingwen Zhu, Ping Li, Qian Zhang, Ge Jin

Unsupervised industrial anomaly detection is widely used because defective samples are scarce while normal data are abundant. Many recent methods follow a feature-embedding pipeline that models patch-level deep features, but they often (i) introduce cross-layer interference when multi-level features are fused and (ii) risk losing fine-grained information when reference features are aggressively reduced. This paper proposes ART-IAD, an online patch-based framework that treats multi-level CNN features as independent views and models each view with an incremental Fuzzy Adaptive Resonance Theory (Fuzzy ART) prototype memory. For each ART prototype, sufficient statistics, including the mean and covariance, are maintained, and Mahalanobis-based anomaly scores are computed, enabling anomaly detection and localization without storing all patch embeddings. On MVTec AD, ART-IAD achieves an average image-level AUROC of 99.4% and pixel-level AUROC of 98.2%, slightly outperforming the strong baseline PatchCore by +0.3% in image-level AUROC and +0.1% in pixel-level AUROC. These results indicate that ART-based online prototype modeling and multi-view separation can provide accurate detection and localization with a compact reference memory.
